paper.title_en: Ensemble equivalence and asymptotic equipartition property in information theory
paper.abstract_en: •Classical information theory corresponds to the canonical ensemble description of information sequences.•The asymptotic equipartition property parallels ensemble equivalence in statistical physics.•Ensemble equivalence guarantees the validity of classical information theory.•Microcanonical Boltzmann entropy sets a new limit of information compression. There is a consensus that information theory and statistical physics have a close relationship but the rigorous proofs are still missing. In this work, according to the statistical ensemble description of the information sequences that are generated by the i.i.d. single variable and multivariate information source, the relationship between the ensemble equivalence and asymptotic equipartition property is established. We find that classical information theory is a special case of the canonical ensemble description from statistical physics. They are both the maximum entropy approximation of the real signal generation. We also find the microcanonical ensemble description is closer to the real signal generation than the conjugate canonical ensemble, but the ensemble equivalence between the microcanonical and canonical ensemble in the thermodynamic limit guarantees the effectiveness of classical information theory, i.e., the asymptotic equipartition property in information theory is an analogue of ensemble equivalence from statistical physics.
